components.name: Ink, Pencil, Struck Entries
components.description: Learned entries carry certainty by writing instrument; striking draws one ruled line left to right and Undo lifts it.
components.html:
• Prefers small reviewable changes.
  • Writes tests before refactors.
  • Works mostly at night.
components.css: .ds-entries { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; font: 400 15px/1.5 Barlow, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; color: var(--ink, #e6ebf2); } .ds-entry { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) auto; gap: 4px 14px; padding: 11px 0 12px; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule, #1f2a3b); } .ds-text { position: relative; justify-self: start; } .ds-entry.ink .ds-text { text-decoration: underline 1.5px var(--blue, #5aa2ff); text-underline-offset: 5px; } .ds-entry.pencil .ds-text { color: var(--pencil, #a7b0bd); text-decoration: underline 1px dashed var(--pencil, #a7b0bd); text-underline-offset: 5px; } .ds-text::after { content: ""; position: absolute; left: -2px; right: -2px; top: 55%; height: 1.5px; background: var(--ink-2, #97a4b6); transform: scaleX(0); transform-origin: left center; transition: transform 0.32s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-entry.struck .ds-text { color: var(--ink-3, #8390a3); } .ds-entry.struck .ds-text::after { transform: scaleX(1); } .ds-strike, .ds-undo { height: 26px; padding: 0 8px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 3px; background: none; color: var(--ink-3, #8390a3); font: 400 12.5px/1 Barlow, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-strike:hover { color: var(--bad, #ff7a6b); border-color: var(--rule-strong, #2c3a50); } .ds-undo { color: var(--blue, #5aa2ff); } .ds-undo:hover { border-color: var(--rule-strong, #2c3a50); } .ds-strike:focus-visible, .ds-undo:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--blue, #5aa2ff); outline-offset: 2px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-text::after { transition: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The interface is a pilot's logbook kept by the machine. Each week is one ruled page: a line per item logged, numbers in fixed columns, totals and brought-forward figures closing the page under double accounting rules, and prose remarks in a margin beside it. The night theme is a cockpit at rest: near-black blue ground, hairline blue-grey rules, paper-white type. The day theme is cool white logbook paper with light blue rules. Both themes are the same page, only the lighting changes.

State is written, not painted. Two writing instruments carry certainty: blue ink underlines what is confirmed, graphite pencil (lighter, dashed underline) marks what is only a candidate. A removal follows logbook law: never erase; a single ruled line is drawn through the entry, which dims but stays legible and restorable. The same principle runs through every status marker: a short rule whose line pattern (solid, dashed, dotted, hairline) carries the meaning, with colour only supporting it.

The system is dense and quiet. Surfaces are flat, square-cornered (3px), and separated by 1px rules rather than shadows or fills. There are no stat cards, no sidebar, no charts beyond single-scale bars. A healthy page has almost no colour on it except blue ink.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled table grammar everywhere: hairline rows, vertical column rules, double rules at head and foot.
Barlow for reading, Barlow Semi Condensed uppercase with tracking for column heads, tabs, and section labels.
Tabular numerals on the whole page.
Blue is the only accent; amber and red appear only for warnings and failures.
Line pattern, never colour alone, distinguishes states.
One fixed attention scale and one week axis across every view.

rules.name: The One Pen Rule
rules.body: Blue is the only accent. Amber and red are signals, not decoration; a healthy week shows neither.

rules.name: The Cool Paper Rule
rules.body: The day theme is cool white paper with blue rules. Never cream, beige, or warm off-white.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is set on the body; every number on every view sits in a fixed-width column.

rules.name: The Stencil Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked text is reserved for the Semi Condensed label roles (column heads, tabs, section headings, kind tags). Body copy, names, and headlines are never set uppercase.

rules.name: The Ruled To The Foot Rule
rules.body: A logbook page never ends in empty panel: blank ruled rows carry the rules down until the totals sit flush on the page frame.

rules.name: The One Axis Rule
rules.body: Every history view uses the same eight-week axis, oldest left, and one fixed attention scale shared across weeks and projects. Bars are never normalised per page.

rules.name: The Double Accounting Rule
rules.body: The log's header and its totals are separated from the body by a 3px double rule in the strong rule colour, as in a ledger. Ordinary rows use 1px hairlines.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: Pages, sheets, and panels never cast shadows; separation is a rule or a paper-tone step.

dos: Do separate everything with rules: 1px hairlines between rows and columns, strong rules under heads, a 3px double rule at the log's head and foot.
Do encode every state as a line pattern first (solid, dashed, dotted, hairline, struck) and let colour only reinforce it.
Do strike removed items with one ruled line and keep them legible with an inline Undo.
Do keep tabular numerals and right-aligned numbers in every numeric column.
Do plot attention on the one fixed scale and the one eight-week axis in every view.
Do fill the log page with blank ruled rows to the foot of the frame when the margin is taller.
Do keep both themes in step: every token has a night value and a cool day value.
donts: Don't use colour alone to distinguish states, candidates, or results.
Don't delete, fade out, or hide a removed entry; strike it.
Don't add stat cards, sidebars, or charts beyond single-scale bars; the page is a logbook, not an admin dashboard.
Don't put shadows on pages, sheets, or panels; the toast is the only floating element.
Don't introduce a second accent hue; amber and red are reserved for warnings and failures.
Don't warm the day theme toward cream or beige.
Don't normalise bars per week or per project.
Don't set body copy, names, or headlines in uppercase; tracked uppercase belongs to the Semi Condensed label roles.
